data.narrative:
General Matter is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Scott Nolan and Lee Robinson that has raised $50M+. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 firms across the nuclear energy sector: three public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private peers including Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $50M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression, yielding $100M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comps—Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A)—produces a median valuation of $808M, with a range of $200M to $6.0B reflecting substantial stage and maturity dispersion.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $85M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $454M. The wide range reflects significant uncertainty around nuclear energy venture valuations at this stage, driven by variable investor expectations for technology risk, regulatory pathway, and capital intensity. The peer-median method anchors toward the upper range given comparable stage comps, while stage-progression implies more conservative progression from capital raised. Key uncertainties include technology validation progress and capital requirements to commercialization.
